abstract.para: While the system you want to back up is running, generate a &rear; recovery system that includes a system-specific recovery installer. This recovery installer can only be used to re-create this specific system. Depending on your backup solution, the recovery system might either include a file backup directly or reference an external file backup.

listitem.para: &rear; is installed on the system you want to back up.

topic.para: Perform this procedure on the original machine:

step.para: Log in either as the &rootuser; user or as a user with sudo privileges.
Create the recovery system, using the -D option to enable verbose mode and debug mode:

listitem.para: For basic backups with tar, use the rear mkbackup command to create both the file backup and the recovery system:
For third-party backup tools, use the rear mkrescue command to create only the recovery system:

step.para: Both commands perform the following steps:

listitem.para: Analyze the system and gather information, particularly about the disk layout (partitioning, file systems, mount points, etc.) and the boot loader.
Create a bootable recovery system with the information gathered in the analysis.

step.para: The rear mkbackup command also calls the internal backup tool to back up system files and user files. The rear mkrescue command doesn't create a backup of the files.
If you used rear mkrescue, create a file backup using your third-party backup tool.
